findings.claim: Said she did not mourn Roe v. Wade’s reversal, stated that Dobbs did not ban abortions, and described it as opening debate to build support for decriminalization.
findings.quote: “Today I don’t mourn the reversal of Roe v. Wade,” Kuniansky told participants. “The Dobbs decision did not ban abortions.” It opened a “debate to win a majority of working people to support decriminalization.”
findings.source_title: Road to women’s emancipation debated at US women’s marches – The Militant
findings.verifier_note: The quote reports Kuniansky’s own statements about Roe, Dobbs, and support for decriminalization.
findings.original_claim: Kuniansky said she did not mourn Roe v. Wade’s reversal, stated that Dobbs did not ban abortions, and described it as opening debate to build support for decriminalization.

findings.claim: In a 2021 statement, Kuniansky argued that government regulations do not stop employers from prioritizing profit over workers and the planet.
findings.quote: Regulations by all-too complicit government bureaucrats do nothing to stop bosses determined to maximize profits at the expense of workers’ lives and our planet.
findings.source_title: Fight for workers control of production! – The Militant
findings.verifier_note: The quote supports her stated view that regulations do not stop employers from prioritizing profits at workers’ and the planet’s expense.

findings.claim: She advocated workers taking control of production, saying that would enable safe work and protect natural resources for future generations.
findings.quote: All work can be performed safely and in ways that protect our natural resources for use by future generations. But for that to become a reality, workers must fight to take control of production out of the bosses’ hands.
findings.source_title: Fight for workers control of production! – The Militant
findings.verifier_note: The quote supports her call for workers to take control of production as a means of making work safe and protecting natural resources.
